clue.text: Rule broken by halfwit put in new position

indicators.note: a word broken by another is split open so the other can sit inside it

blocks.note: to reign is to rule
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A ruler's authority is undermined by a fool who has been moved to a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: Halfwit is not asking for half a word here: it is simply a fool, and the rule is split open to hold him.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign someone is to transfer them to a different post or role.

clue.text: OT prophet endlessly pursuing king’s pleasure

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off
pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
Elisha is an Old Testament prophet, successor to Elijah

explanation.surface: An Old Testament prophet chases after a king's delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of king's is part of the surface; the definition is the noun pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish means enjoyment or zest, as in eating with relish, a synonym for pleasure.

clue.text: Uphold placing a female over company

indicators.note: placing one thing over another in a down entry puts it on top, so earlier in the word

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for female
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A firm backs a policy of putting a woman in charge of the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm a decision is to confirm or support it, as a court upholds a ruling.

clue.text: Reconstruct a buttress for lower level

indicators.note: to reconstruct is to build again in a new form, so these letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: An instruction to rebuild a wall support so that it sits lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: A substrate is an underlying layer, such as the base material beneath a surface coating or soil beneath topsoil.

clue.text: Good diversion set up in poll that may accompany proposal

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top
in tells us one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
fun is amusement or diversion
a poll is an election

explanation.surface: A political tale of good distraction staged during an election, which may accompany some policy proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: The proposal is not political but a marriage proposal, traditionally made down on one knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A genuflection is a bending of the knee, the gesture a suitor makes when asking someone to marry them.

clue.text: Bone that always has one end in the centre

definitions.text: that always has one end in the centre

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the two long bones of the forearm

blocks.clueFragment: that always has one end in the centre
blocks.note: second meaning: a line from the middle of a circle out to its edge

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as a riddle about the bone, but it describes the geometric line, which runs from the centre of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a forearm bone and the straight line joining a circle's middle to its circumference.

clue.text: Finally reduced world records

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the phrase goes

blocks.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: At long last, the global records have been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: World records sounds like sporting achievements; here it is a book recording the world.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps that charts the countries of the globe.

clue.text: Without costume, cross water

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: cross means angry
a rig, or rig-out, is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: Someone without their costume is annoyed, or is about to swim across water.
explanation.walkthrough: Without reads as lacking, but its older meaning is outside, so the angry word wraps the outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To water a field is to irrigate it, supplying crops with moisture through channels or pipes.

clue.text: Collective punishment? Certainly not

blocks.note: surface reading: a denial that a whole group is being penalised
setter's reading: the opposite of collective is alone, so the punishment is confinement apart from all other prisoners

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'certainly not' as the opposite of collective: a prison punishment that is the reverse of a group one.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary, short for solitary confinement, is a punishment in which a prisoner is kept entirely alone.

clue.text: Part of foreign capital deposited with financial institution

blocks.note: something deposited has been left somewhere
a bank is a financial institution

explanation.surface: Money from abroad is paid into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about money, but the capital is a city: Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank is the southern district of Paris, famous for artists and cafés, so a section of a foreign capital city.

clue.text: As fish may be, but not bird or mammal

definitions.text: As fish may be, but not bird or mammal

blocks.clueFragment: As fish may be, but not bird or mammal
blocks.note: surface reading: a biology question about some property fish have and other animals lack

blocks.clueFragment: As fish may be, but not bird or mammal
blocks.note: setter's reading: grammar, since the word fish can name many fish, while bird and mammal each name only one

explanation.walkthrough: Think about the words, not the creatures: fish serves as its own multiple form, but bird and mammal are always singular as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural describes a word form denoting more than one, which fish can do unchanged while bird and mammal cannot.

clue.text: It’s in support I and a Conservative assembled for appeasing

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the pieces are joined in sequence

blocks.note: a prop is a support
taken as written; the 's in reads as 'is in', placing it after the support
taken as written
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political pledge of backing from a Tory, offered to calm things down.
explanation.definitionFit: Propitiatory means intended to win favour or soothe anger, so serving to placate someone.

clue.text: Supporter‘s trust slightly disturbed, with second coming first

indicators.note: only slightly disturbed means the order is changed a little, by moving a single letter
second is S by abbreviation, and coming first says exactly which letter moves and where to: to the front

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan's confidence is shaken a little when a runner-up suddenly takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says how the letters move: second (S, its usual abbreviation) comes first, so the S of TRUST jumps to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a bar or brace that holds up part of a structure, so a physical support.

clue.text: Planning on behalf of crew about start of strike

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only
about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: doing something for someone is acting on their behalf
a rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called an eight
the opening letter of strike

explanation.surface: A union plans ahead on its members' behalf before a strike begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew stands for a rowing eight; the S slips in after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the habit of looking ahead and preparing, which is close to forward planning.

clue.text: Trips learner, shattering computer peripheral

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into fragments, so the letters are smashed and remade

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A novice stumbles over a piece of office equipment and breaks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser printer is an output device attached to a computer, the kind of add-on hardware called a peripheral.

clue.text: Turning over stylish reading

blocks.note: something in is fashionable
a reading of a text is one version or interpretation of it

explanation.surface: Flipping through a fashionable book.
explanation.definitionFit: An inversion is the act of turning something upside down or reversing its order.

clue.text: Person losing faith — a part of body has run out

indicators.note: has run out means the run has left, so its letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
the prostate is a gland in the male body
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning their beliefs because a part of their body has given up.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who renounces their religion or former principles.

clue.text: Overtake European in odd display of par golf

indicators.note: an odd display is a strange showing, so these letters appear in an unusual order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A European golfer passes a rival during an unusual round played at par.
explanation.definitionFit: To leapfrog a rival is to jump ahead of them, as in the children's game of vaulting over backs.

clue.text: Contest held by idiot the writer has planned to avoid

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

blocks.note: a prat is a fool in British slang
a sporting event is a contest
the writer is the setter, I, so the writer has is I've

explanation.surface: A competition run by a fool, which the author has arranged to sidestep.
explanation.walkthrough: Prat is British slang for a foolish person; 'the writer' is the setter speaking of themself, so 'the writer has' is I've.
explanation.definitionFit: Preventative describes measures intended to stop something happening, so designed for averting trouble.

clue.text: Where credibility helps? It may stand without further probe, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letters are kept
without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: stet, Latin for let it stand, is the proofreader's mark cancelling a correction
the final letters of further and probe

explanation.surface: A detective's reputation counts for something, and a case may hold without any more investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: Credibility here is the cred in street cred, standing among ordinary people; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Street credibility is respect among fashionable urban young people, so the street is where that credibility counts.

clue.text: Reference work that’s turned up, figuratively speaking

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped to read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to cite a source is to reference it
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A reference book that has surfaced, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic language uses imagery and metaphor, the same as speaking in figures rather than literally.

clue.text: Pressure inside Venus or a wildly exploding star

indicators.note: acting wildly means behaving without order, so these letters are scrambled
inside tells us one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the letters of all three words
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure builds up within Venus or some other body until it bursts like a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is the enormous explosion of a dying star, making it briefly very bright.

clue.text: Cook in pan

blocks.note: first meaning: to bake meat in an oven
second meaning: to criticise harshly

explanation.walkthrough: Cook in pan reads as a kitchen instruction; pan is really a verb for slating a show or book.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to cook meat in dry heat and to criticise severely, as a reviewer might.

clue.text: First of all, routinely attend thus in office — nine to five, say

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every word that follows

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Above all, turn up regularly at work and keep normal office hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine to five looks like working hours, but here it is read as numbers compared, 9:5.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine to five can be written 9:5, an example of a ratio comparing two quantities.

clue.text: A minor thoroughfare, not in this country

blocks.note: taken as written
British roads are graded A (main) and B (secondary), so a minor road is a B-class one

explanation.surface: A little back road is said to be found in another land.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means overseas, in a foreign land rather than at home.

clue.text: Part of scale that is least fragile

blocks.note: sol (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa musical scale
id est is the Latin behind the abbreviation i.e.

explanation.surface: Some section of a set of scales is the sturdiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid things are firm and strong, so the most solid is the opposite of the most breakable.

clue.text: Score less than century — that’s significant after losing first wicket

indicators.note: losing its first means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: something weighty is important
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A batsman's score falls short of a hundred, a big deal after an early wicket goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so a hundred less a score is the number wanted; the cricket scene hides this arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: One hundred minus twenty, the old counting word score, comes to the number eighty.

clue.text: Compelling reform of phony movement out of control

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A persuasive call to overhaul a fake campaign that has run riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hypnotic holds attention irresistibly, as a mesmerising performance does.
